newsitem.title: THAILAND: FOCUS-Thai rates seen easing - central bank chief.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Thai rates seen easing - central bank chief.

text.p: Thailand's central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Monday that he expected local commercial banks to cut their rates in coming weeks.
"The central bank sees local commercial banks cutting deposit rates further in the next two to three weeks which will eventually lead to cuts in lending rates," he told reporters.

The governor said the interest rate might be cut by 25 basis points initially and will come down further, but he declined to say what interest rate level would be deemed appropriate by the central bank.
"It depends on the market mechanism and the economic situation," Rerngchai said.
Thailand's lending rates are among the highest in the region and range between 13.0 and 13.25 percent.
Shortly after the governor made his remarks, two leading Thai banks said they would reduce their lending rates by 25 basis points.
Krung Thai Bank Plc and Siam Commercial Bank said their rate cuts will be effective on Tuesday.
After the cuts, the new minimum lending rate (MLR) at Krung Thai Bank will be 12.75 percent while the new MLR at Siam Commercial Bank will be 13.00 percent, company officials said.

Private analysts have blamed high interest rates for some of the country's economic ills which range from a turmoil-ridden finance sector to a depressed property sector, and a slowdown in exports, private investment and manufacturing activity.
Some analysts said last week they expected banks to cut rates by between 50 to 100 basis points this year after Rerngchai first said on Friday that rates could come down.
Earlier on Monday, Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said the sluggish Thai economy was stabilising now but it would take time for a recovery.

"The economy has improved but it needs more time to recover. It won't take a day or two to solve all the problems," Amnuay said. "If you look at economic history of other countries, you'll see that is the case."
Official predictions are that the problem-ridden Thai economy will grow by 6.8 percent this year but private analysts expect it to be well below six percent.
